picks.style: archaic greek hymn, phorminx lyre and frame drum, bright rhapsode tenor, steady processional, incantatory
picks.why: The invocation plus the litany of epithets — robber, cattle driver, bringer of dreams, watcher by night — is a built-in refrain.

picks.style: playful greek lyre song, solo kithara with hand percussion, light agile tenor, quick, mischievous, dancing
picks.why: The birth of the lyre itself: strings tried one by one, and the god singing his own begetting in sweet random snatches.

picks.style: greek hymn of wonder, layered lyre and soft aulos, warm high voice, slow, rapt, swelling
picks.why: Apollo undone by music — 'mirth, and love, and sweet sleep' is the line the whole hymn turns on.

picks.style: old english alliterative chant, bowed lyre and low drone, deep male voice, hushed then rising, visionary
picks.why: The dream of the Rood in the night camp — a tree of glory with letters of light laced upon it.

picks.style: nordic folk war-verse, bowed lyre and frame drum, stark low chant, driving, cold, martial
picks.why: Banners billowing, byrnies glittering, oaths of slaughter on the Danube's dark bank — hard alliterative drive.

picks.style: solitary old english lament, single bowed lyre, aged male voice, very slow, bare, inward
picks.why: The poet's own signature: old and ready for his journey, weaving word-craft in the narrow night.

picks.style: georgian pastoral air, harpsichord and recorder, clear light soprano, lilting, gentle, dancing
picks.why: A true song in tetrameter — rivers, roses, woodbine, and Zephyr called to waft rest to Mira's breast.

picks.style: georgian parlour song, harpsichord and viola da gamba, expressive mezzo, measured, wistful, chamber
picks.why: Dorinda at her glass: 'the fading Roses die, / And the last Sparkles tremble in her Eye.'

picks.style: english baroque devotional air, chamber organ and lute, warm soprano, unhurried, bright, contemplative
picks.why: 'There's not a Seed but what contains a Flower' — and with each plump fruit we swallow down a tree.

picks.style: georgian pastoral ode, baroque strings and recorder, warm tenor, flowing, fresh, morning-bright
picks.why: Milk-maid, flail, and the lark that soars upright and sings at the gate of heaven.

picks.style: english pastoral ballad, acoustic strings and soft flute, warm low voice, unhurried, dusk-lit, fading
picks.why: New-mown hay, blackbird on the spray, 'the calm farewel of parting light, / And Ev'ning sad'ning into Night.'

picks.style: sublime baroque ode, full strings and chamber organ, declamatory tenor, stately, swelling, awed
picks.why: The moon as empress with a thousand hand-maid stars, stirring the ocean to rebel against her sister Earth.

picks.style: late antique latin recitation, soft harp and low strings, avuncular baritone, measured, warm, conversational
picks.why: The only candidate, and it carries a real turn: a grandfather telling a frightened boy that the schoolmaster's terror is only painted scenery.

picks.style: hellenistic bucolic idyll, panpipes and soft lyre, high tenor, languid, honeyed, tender
picks.why: Achilles veiled among the girls at the loom — 'the heart of a man he had, and the love of a man he had.'

picks.style: sicilian pastoral duet, syrinx and plucked lyre, two soft voices trading lines, gentle, sunlit, unhurried
picks.why: A shepherd asking for a song and naming exactly what he wants: the Scyrian love, the secret kisses, the secret bed.

picks.style: archaic greek soldier's song, aulos and hand drum, wry baritone, brisk, marching, defiant
picks.why: Archilochus thrown out of Sparta, with the shield poem itself intact — 'no worse surely I'll get the next time.'

picks.style: latin epode dirge, low male chorus and sparse frame drum, slow, ominous, unresolved
picks.why: The only candidate in the work — a bleak Horatian tag on fratricide that at least stands alone as a line.
